actions.title: One tail is enough to work on.
actions.summary: Work backward from the two-sided endpoint. It suffices to obtain an upper-tail estimate for an arbitrary matrix, then apply it again to −A.
actions.need: Control deviations both above and below the mean.
actions.have: The theorem permits every real A, and both matrix norms are unchanged by a sign.
actions.observation: Replacing A by −A turns Q into −Q without changing V or L. The lower tail is another instance of the same upper-tail problem.
actions.check: The sign-reversal choice is strategic. Verifying the identity and the event union is basic. Numerical prefactors are adjusted at the end.
actions.tool: Union bound; homogeneity of operator and Frobenius norms.

actions.title: Read the quadratic form coordinate by coordinate.
actions.summary: Expand what is already given. Independence and zero means eliminate off-diagonal terms from the expectation.
actions.need: Find usable structure in the centered quadratic form.
actions.observation: For i ≠ j, the given independence directly permits 𝔼(XᵢXⱼ) = 𝔼Xᵢ 𝔼Xⱼ = 0. This observation supports a basic inference, not a new strategic construction.
actions.math:
Q = D + S
D = Σᵢ aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²)
S = Σᵢ≠ⱼ aᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ
actions.check: The equality is direct expansion. Choosing to give D and S different proof methods is the next strategic decision.
actions.tool: Expectation factorization for independent variables; linearity of expectation.

actions.title: Give the two kinds of terms different jobs.
actions.summary: The upper-tail goal branches. Bound D and S at threshold t/2. The diagonal branch is a side checkpoint; the main track follows the harder cross terms.
actions.need: A bound for ℙ(D + S ≥ t).
actions.have: The identity Q = D + S. Terms in D use separate coordinates; terms in S can share them.
actions.observation: Only the diagonal sum preserves independence term by term. Separating it lets Bernstein handle the easy branch while we develop a different tool for the cross terms.
actions.check: This is a sufficient-condition reduction. D and S need not be independent. Choosing the split and thresholds is strategic; the event inclusion is basic logic.
actions.tool: Union bound; knowledge of the input conditions for Bernstein and decoupling.

actions.title: Close the diagonal branch with Bernstein.
actions.summary: The square of a subgaussian is subexponential. Centering preserves that control, and the diagonal summands are independent.
actions.need: An exponential bound for the diagonal sum D.
actions.have: Independent variables Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ², each with subexponential norm at most CK².
actions.observation: Bernstein accepts independent centered subexponential summands and produces exactly a minimum of quadratic and linear scales—the shape the endpoint asks for.
actions.math:
‖Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²‖ψ₁ ≤ CK²
Σᵢ aᵢᵢ² ≤ ‖A‖F²,   maxᵢ ∣aᵢᵢ∣ ≤ ‖A‖
ℙ(D ≥ t/2) ≤ exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}]
actions.check: Check independence, centering and subexponential sizes before applying Bernstein. If the diagonal is zero, D is zero and the positive-threshold bound is immediate.
actions.tool: Subgaussian-square and subexponential-centering bounds; Bernstein inequality.

actions.title: Ask for an exponential moment instead of a tail.
actions.summary: Choose a transform whose expectation the toolkit can control. An MGF bound over a restricted parameter range will be enough.
actions.have: The coordinates come with subgaussian exponential-moment bounds, but S itself has dependent summands.
actions.observation: Exponentiation turns a tail event into an expectation problem. A quadratic MGF bound gives the t²/V regime; a cutoff λ ≲ 1/L supplies the t/L regime.
actions.math:
ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/2) 𝔼exp(λS)
New goal: 𝔼exp(λS) ≤ exp(CVλ²)
for 0 < λ ≤ c₀/L.
actions.check: Apply Markov to the nonnegative variable exp(λS). This yields an upper bound, not equality between the tail and MGF. We will choose λ only after establishing its allowed range.

actions.category: Toolkit application after direct hypothesis checks
actions.title: Prepare the linear-form bound.
actions.summary: The starting assumptions already control any fixed linear combination of the coordinates.
actions.need: A reusable bound when the coefficients of a linear form become fixed.
actions.observation: For a fixed vector v, exponentiating a sum makes a product. Independence factors its expectation, and the scalar subgaussian MGF applies to every factor.
actions.check: The scalar MGF bound is an available theorem. Factoring the expectation, substituting its inputs, and summing the exponent are its verification steps. The mean-zero condition matters here.

actions.title: Make one side possible to hold fixed.
actions.summary: Introduce an independent copy X′. Decoupling bounds the off-diagonal exponential moment by a bilinear form involving two independent vectors.
actions.need: Use linear-form MGF control on the cross terms.
actions.have: S = Σᵢ≠ⱼaᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ. Shared coordinates block a direct independent-sum argument.
actions.observation: In XᵀAX, holding one copy of X fixed also freezes the other. In XᵀAX′, conditioning on X′ leaves a genuine random linear form in X.
actions.math:
𝔼exp(λS) ≤ 𝔼exp(4λXᵀAX′)
Conditional on X′: XᵀAX′ = 〈X, AX′〉.
actions.check: This is a convex-function comparison, not equality in law. One construction randomly splits indices into disjoint groups: each off-diagonal pair survives with probability 1/4. Jensen and zero conditional means give the factor 4. The full A is allowed on the right by the off-diagonal version of the theorem.
actions.tool: Decoupling, Theorem 6.1.1 and Remark 6.1.2; Jensen inequality.

actions.title: Recognize a Gaussian formula inside the bound.
actions.summary: The decoupled expression suggests conditioning. Its conditional subgaussian upper bound has the same form as an exact Gaussian MGF.
actions.have: After conditioning, v = AX′ is fixed, and a bound of the form exp(CK²λ²‖v‖²) is available.
actions.observation: A Gaussian linear form has MGF exp(μ²‖v‖²/2). Choosing μ proportional to Kλ matches the entire expression, not just its general shape.
actions.math:
𝔼g exp(μ〈g,v〉) = exp(μ²‖v‖²/2)
Choose μ = √(2C)Kλ.
New subgoal: bound 𝔼exp(θgᵀAg′), with θ = CK²λ.
actions.check: This step proposes the replacement and a new sufficient goal. The forward replacement must still verify the comparison in both arguments.
actions.tool: Gaussian linear MGF; Gaussian replacement, Lemma 6.2.3.

actions.title: Carry out the two Gaussian replacements.
actions.summary: Condition on X′ and use the prepared linear bound to replace X by g at cost CK. Then condition on g and replace X′ by an independent g′ at another cost CK.
actions.need: Transfer the MGF problem to a distribution whose rotations we understand.
actions.have: The decoupled bilinear form and the fixed-coefficient subgaussian MGF bound.
actions.observation: Each replacement becomes a one-vector linear-form calculation when the other vector is fixed. Two such comparisons produce a parameter of order K²λ.
actions.math:
𝔼exp(4λXᵀAX′)
≤ 𝔼exp(CK²λ gᵀAg′),
g,g′ independent standard Gaussian vectors.
actions.check: Iterated expectation lifts each conditional comparison. Constants absorb the factor 4 from decoupling. No coordinate-wise equality in distribution between X and g is claimed.
actions.tool: Subgaussian linear MGF; Gaussian MGF; iterated expectation.

actions.title: Rotate until the matrix exposes independent products.
actions.summary: Choose the singular value decomposition A = U diag(sᵢ)Vᵀ. The Gaussian subgoal becomes a product of scalar MGFs.
actions.need: A Gaussian MGF controlled by ‖A‖F and ‖A‖.
actions.have: Independent standard Gaussian vectors and a fixed matrix A.
actions.observation: An arbitrary rotation could destroy independence for the original X. Gaussian rotation preserves independent standard coordinates. The resulting singular values give both target norms.
actions.math:
gᵀAg′ ≡in law Σᵢ sᵢgᵢgᵢ′
𝔼exp(θgᵀAg′) = ∏ᵢ 𝔼exp(θsᵢgᵢgᵢ′)
Σᵢsᵢ² = ‖A‖F²,   maxᵢsᵢ = ‖A‖.
actions.check: SVD is valid for a nonsymmetric real A too: use Uᵀg and Vᵀg′. Their independent standard Gaussian laws are preserved. This is why replacement precedes rotation.
actions.tool: SVD; Gaussian rotation invariance; independence; singular-value norm identities.

actions.category: Basic calculation supported by Gaussian toolkit
actions.title: Compute the scalar MGF and its domain.
actions.summary: The scalar target now has a direct calculation. Conditioning once reduces it to the MGF of a squared Gaussian.
actions.need: The product bound anticipated by the goal layer.
actions.have: Independent pairs (gᵢ,gᵢ′) and the representation Σᵢsᵢgᵢgᵢ′.
actions.observation: The exponent is linear in gᵢ′ when gᵢ is fixed. Its conditional MGF becomes exp(u²gᵢ²/2), whose expectation is explicit.
actions.math:
𝔼exp(ugg′) = (1 − u²)⁻¹ᐟ²
≤ exp(u²)  when u² ≤ 1/2.
𝔼exp(θgᵀAg′) ≤ exp(θ²‖A‖F²)
for ∣θ∣ ≤ 1/(√2 ‖A‖).
actions.check: The bound uses −½log(1−u²) ≤ u² on [0,1/2]. The largest singular value controls the admissible θ; the sum of squares controls the exponent. Both are necessary.
actions.tool: Gaussian linear and square MGFs; the elementary logarithm bound.

actions.category: Basic substitution · the two layers meet
actions.title: The derived MGF meets the requested MGF.
actions.summary: Substitute θ = CK²λ into the Gaussian estimate, and chain it with the two forward comparisons. This is the main connection between the two layers.
actions.need: 𝔼exp(λS) ≤ exp(CVλ²) for λ at most c₀/L.
actions.have: Decoupling, Gaussian replacement, and the computed Gaussian-product MGF.
actions.observation: The forward chain has produced exactly the kind of bound requested by the backward Chernoff goal—including the parameter restriction. This checkpoint can now be discharged.
actions.math:
𝔼 exp(λS) ≤ 𝔼 exp(4λXᵀAX′)
≤ 𝔼 exp(CK²λgᵀAg′)
≤ exp(CK⁴λ²‖A‖F²) = exp(CVλ²),
for ∣λ∣ ≤ c₀/(K²‖A‖) = c₀/L.
actions.check: The constant c₀ includes all rescalings. A domain restriction on θ must be converted into a domain restriction on λ; it cannot be dropped.
actions.tool: The three established estimates; substitution and inequality transitivity.

actions.title: Balance the exponent, respecting the cutoff.
actions.summary: Choose the smaller of the unconstrained balancing scale and an allowed MGF scale. Two different reasons for stopping λ produce the two tail regimes.
actions.need: Turn the exponential-moment estimate into the desired tail.
actions.have: ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/2 + CVλ²), for 0 < λ ≤ c₀/L.
actions.observation: The positive quadratic term must stay smaller than the negative linear term. Increasing λ helps only until balancing or the MGF cutoff stops us.
actions.math:
λ = min{t/(4CV), c₀/(2L)}
CVλ² ≤ λt/4
ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/4)
≤ exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}].
actions.check: If t/(4CV) is smaller, the exponent is quadratic in t. If the cutoff is smaller, it is linear in t. This explicitly discharges the off-diagonal tail goal.
actions.tool: Chernoff estimate already established; elementary parameter comparison.

actions.category: Basic logic & constants after the strategic plan
actions.title: Both branches reach the original endpoint.
actions.summary: Combine the diagonal and off-diagonal tails. Apply the same result to −A and use the union bound. Every goal checkpoint is now supported.
actions.need: The original two-sided bound, with prefactor 2.
actions.have: Both upper-tail branches, the sign-reversal reduction, and unchanged matrix norms under A ↦ −A.
actions.observation: The only remaining mismatch is the prefactor: splitting terms and signs gives 4 instead of 2. Combining with the universal bound ℙ ≤ 1 absorbs it into a smaller exponent constant.
actions.check: For q ≤ 2log(2)/c the last expression is at least 1; for larger q the comparison with 4exp(−cq) holds. The theorem follows for all t; degenerate cases were handled at the start.
actions.tool: Union bound; the diagonal and off-diagonal bounds; elementary inequalities.

context.scope: For the displayed derivation assume t > 0 and V,L > 0. The zero cases are immediate. Definitions and calculation are basic; choosing a useful representation or theorem is strategic.

facts.title: Read the quadratic form coordinate by coordinate.
facts.statement:
Q = D + S
D = Σᵢ aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²)
S = Σᵢ≠ⱼ aᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ
facts.verification: The equality is direct expansion. Choosing to give D and S different proof methods is the next strategic decision.

facts.title: Prepare the linear-form bound.
facts.statement:
𝔼exp(λ〈X,v〉) = ∏ᵢ 𝔼exp(λvᵢXᵢ)
≤ ∏ᵢ exp(CK²λ²vᵢ²)
= exp(CK²λ²‖v‖₂²)
facts.verification: The scalar MGF bound is an available theorem. Factoring the expectation, substituting its inputs, and summing the exponent are its verification steps. The mean-zero condition matters here.

facts.title: Make one side possible to hold fixed.
facts.statement:
𝔼exp(λS) ≤ 𝔼exp(4λXᵀAX′)
Conditional on X′: XᵀAX′ = 〈X, AX′〉.
facts.verification: This is a convex-function comparison, not equality in law. One construction randomly splits indices into disjoint groups: each off-diagonal pair survives with probability 1/4. Jensen and zero conditional means give the factor 4. The full A is allowed on the right by the off-diagonal version of the theorem.

facts.title: Carry out the two Gaussian replacements.
facts.statement:
𝔼exp(4λXᵀAX′)
≤ 𝔼exp(CK²λ gᵀAg′),
g,g′ independent standard Gaussian vectors.
facts.verification: Iterated expectation lifts each conditional comparison. Constants absorb the factor 4 from decoupling. No coordinate-wise equality in distribution between X and g is claimed.

facts.title: Compute the scalar MGF and its domain.
facts.statement:
𝔼exp(ugg′) = (1 − u²)⁻¹ᐟ²
≤ exp(u²)  when u² ≤ 1/2.
𝔼exp(θgᵀAg′) ≤ exp(θ²‖A‖F²)
for ∣θ∣ ≤ 1/(√2 ‖A‖).
facts.verification: The bound uses −½log(1−u²) ≤ u² on [0,1/2]. The largest singular value controls the admissible θ; the sum of squares controls the exponent. Both are necessary.

facts.title: The derived MGF meets the requested MGF.
facts.statement:
𝔼 exp(λS) ≤ 𝔼 exp(4λXᵀAX′)
≤ 𝔼 exp(CK²λgᵀAg′)
≤ exp(CK⁴λ²‖A‖F²) = exp(CVλ²),
for ∣λ∣ ≤ c₀/(K²‖A‖) = c₀/L.
facts.verification: The constant c₀ includes all rescalings. A domain restriction on θ must be converted into a domain restriction on λ; it cannot be dropped.

facts.title: Balance the exponent, respecting the cutoff.
facts.statement:
λ = min{t/(4CV), c₀/(2L)}
CVλ² ≤ λt/4
ℙ(S ≥ t/2) ≤ exp(−λt/4)
≤ exp[−c min{t²/V, t/L}].
facts.verification: If t/(4CV) is smaller, the exponent is quadratic in t. If the cutoff is smaller, it is linear in t. This explicitly discharges the off-diagonal tail goal.
